names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 8 Ιανουαρίου, «Όσιος Αγαθών», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's fourth heading for the Julian 2 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Преподобни Агатон.“, with the rank word Преподобни left off. The heading gives no epithet; Egypt and the century are in the body.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 2 марта ст. ст., name page 62, «Агафон Скитский (египетский), пустынник», with the rank and office words left off. Both epithets are part of the name the calendar’s index carries and both stay, the second in the brackets and the lower case the source itself gives it; the day’s own line has instead «Агафона Египетского», the forename declined with one epithet. `.tmp/foldchk.py` reports no folder holding this form and none holding the bare «Агафон».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 2 марта ст. ст. — «Прп. Агафона Египетского (V).»

attestations.note: The Greek calendar keeps him on 8 January and this one, with the Serbian Охридски пролог, on the Julian 2 March; the two menologion numbers are two calendars’ own and neither is a conversion of the other, and each row records its own day.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 15.03.2026 (2. март ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Агатон.“

attestations.note: The corpus keeps this folder on the Greek 8 Ιανουαρίου and the Prologue keeps him on the Julian 2 March. The two entries are read as one man: both describe an ascetic of the desert with no see, no monastery and no year, whose sayings are those of the Gerontikon, and neither page offers an epithet or a place that would tell two Agathons of that description apart. The Prologue adds what saint.gr has not — Egypt, the fifth century, and Lot as his teacher — and the corpus already keeps that Lot, on the Greek 22 Οκτωβρίου, as a wise ascetic of the desert whose sayings are in the Paradise of the Fathers. Two churches keeping a desert father on two different days is the ordinary case and is not a second feast on one church. The identification is a reading and is in the reader's report.

floruit.note: The Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the Julian 2 March: „Преподобни Агатон, велики мисирски подвижник из V века.“ It gives the century and no year. The folder carried no dates at all before this reading, and saint.gr, the only other source read for him, gives him no year, no country and no monastery. days.pravoslavie.ru closes its own line with «(V)», the same century.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru: «Преподобный Агафон преставился около 435 года». It is the only year of the three sources read for him, it falls inside the fifth century the Охридски пролог gives, and the «около» is the source’s own, so the bound is kept approximate and the floruit is left as it stood.
